t: Section 8104(a)(3)(B) is amended by striking “$600,000” and inserting “$1,000,000”.

fable.w: This section only amends a dollar threshold in an existing statute, replacing $600,000 with $1,000,000. No tempting reading exists: it mentions no consultation, hearing, rulemaking, advisory body, or right to sue, and no party outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that raises a dollar threshold from $600,000 to $1,000,000. It sets up no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue. Even if the threshold decides when Congress must approve a project, Congress is inside the federal government, so that would not count as participation.
opus.s: Section 8104(a)(3)(B) is amended by striking “$600,000” and inserting “$1,000,000”.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting wrong reading:** The cited provision, 38 U.S.C. 8104, deals with congressional authorization of VA medical facility projects. That might suggest some procedural review. It fails because the amendment only changes a dollar threshold. Any approval it affects is by Congress, which is inside the federal government. No outside party is consulted, given a hearing, or given a right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a simple legislative amendment changing a monetary figure. It does not establish any mechanism for consultation, coordination, or input from parties outside the federal government. There is no mention of public hearings, advisory committees, state/tribal consultation, or comment periods.
qwen_chat.s: Section 8104(a)(3)(B) is amended by striking “$600,000” and inserting “$1,000,000”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that changing a dollar amount could affect who gets grants or benefits, thus involving outside parties. However, the text itself is merely a technical amendment to a statutory cap. It does not describe any process of consultation, hearing, comment period, or advisory committee involving non-federal actors. It is a legislative directive to change a number, not a procedural requirement for participation.
